---
title: "Overview"
guide-section: "User Guide"
---

`py-lic-dsf` is an **unofficial** Python implementation of the
[IMF/World Bank Debt Sustainability Framework for Low-Income Countries](https://www.worldbank.org/en/programs/debt-toolkit/dsf).
It is under active construction and should be treated as an unstable alpha.

Created by [Teal Insights](https://tealinsights.com/) and
[Nature Finance](https://www.naturefinance.net/), it targets the official
August 12, 2025
["New LIC-DSF template (Excel file)"](https://thedocs.worldbank.org/en/doc/f0ade6bcf85b6f98dbeb2c39a2b7770c-0360012025/original/LIC-DSF-IDA21-Template-08-12-2025-vf.xlsm).

The user workflow is:

> edit the country workbook in Excel → call the relevant `load_*` function or
> `compute_outputs` → inspect or export pandas panels

## Reading order

| Page | Result |
|------|--------|
| [Getting started](01-getting-started.qmd) | Install, choose loaders, and export a sidecar workbook |
| [Baseline DSA](02-baseline-dsa.qmd) | Output 1-1 / 1-2 |
| [Stress DSA](03-stress-dsa.qmd) | Output 3-1 / 3-2 |
| [Realism](04-realism.qmd) | Output 4 |
| [Risk rating](05-risk-rating.qmd) | Output 5-1 / 5-2 |
| [Probability](06-probability.qmd) | Output 6 |
| [Risk rating summary](07-risk-summary.qmd) | Output 7 |

Each analysis page has a runnable recipe and a paired notebook. Contributors
maintaining formulas and Excel parity should use the **Developer Guide**.

## Template and license

The repository includes
[`data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/lic-dsf-template-2025-08-12.xlsx).
Point the loaders at your filled country workbook with the same sheet layout.

MIT covers the Python source. The template remains an IMF/World Bank work; see
[`NOTICE.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/NOTICE.md)
and
[`data/PROVENANCE.md`](https://github.com/Teal-Insights/py-lic-dsf/blob/main/data/PROVENANCE.md).
